answer: An attester must stake 18% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a inexpensive one. Because the terrace stake is held until the bridge settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the lagoon audit lists each exposure. A farm running 83 keys therefore forfeits that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation low-cost. That is 32 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
